newsitem.title: UK: EIU sees rising world wheat output, consumption.
newsitem.headline: EIU sees rising world wheat output, consumption.

text.p: World wheat production will rise to 605 million tonnes in 1998, from 590 in 1997 and 581 in 1996, according to the Economist Intelligence Unit.
Consumption will rise from 574 million tonnes in 1996-97 to 588 million in 1997/98 and 603 million in 1998/99.

In its World Commodity Forecasts: food feedstuffs and beverages report for the second quarter of 1997, the EIU predicted production in China rising from 108 million tonnes in 1996, to 111 million in 1997 and 113 million in 1998.
China's consumption will rise from 118 million tonnes in 1996-97 to 120 million in 1997-98 and 123 million in 1988-99, the EIU said.

But EU production will first rise, from 99 million in 1996 to 102 million in 1997 and then fall to 98 million in 1998, according to the EIU. EU consumption will rise from 82 million tonnes in 1996-97 to 83 million in 1997-98 and then stay at 83 million in 1988-99, the EIU said.
Increasing stocks will encourage EU agriculture ministers to set a much higher set-aside, probably 15 per cent for the 1998 crop, the EIU said.

The EIU predicted a rise in U.S. production from 62 million tones in 1996, to 63 million in 1997 and 66 million in 1998. U.S. consumption is seen stable at 36 million tonnes 1996-97 and 1997-98 and rising to 37 million in 1988-99, the EIU said.

India's production will rise from 63 million tonnes in 1996, to 66 million in 1997 and 67 million in 1998. India's consumption will rise from 66 million tonnes in 1996-97 to 67 million in 1997-98 and 68 million in 1988-99, the EIU said.
